```{r setup}
library(centraldogma)
```

This package mimics the central dogma of molecular biology. It takes a piece of DNA, then transcribe it into RNA, and then translate it into a protein/string of amino acids.

The first function of the package create_dna_string works by creating random DNA sequence of a length determined by the input. Here we input 30 to get a DNA sequence of length 30:

```{r}
dna_string = create_dna_string(30)
dna_string
```

The second function of the package dna_to_rna is used to substitute the "T"s with "U"s in a given DNA string. So reusing the DNA string we just created we can convert or DNA to RNA:

```{r}
rna_string = dna_to_rna(dna_string)
rna_string
```

The third function of the package split_into_codons creates a character vector of codons from an RNA string, where it is possible to change the start position or use the default start of 1:

```{r}
codon_vector = split_into_codons(rna_string)
codon_vector
```

The fourth function of the package INSERT_NAME takes a character vector of codons and uses the package data codon_table to convert the codons to a string of letters symbolizing amino acids:

```{r}
# aa_sequence = INSERT_NAME(codon_vector)
# aa_sequence
```

The fifth and final function of the package plot_aa_count takes a string input of amino acids, then it counts how many times the present amino acids are in the sequence and plots the counts using ggplot2::geom_col():

```{r}
# count_plot = plot_aa_count(aa_sequence)
# count_plot
```
